# Build a roadmap

Use the requested field of study as the input. Check `src/catalog.js` for existing fields and slugs; avoid duplicate artifacts. Read [roadmap-workflow.md](references/roadmap-workflow.md) for the detailed research, artifact structure, and quality requirements. All project paths are relative to the repository root.

1. Research current education pathways, tools and AI adoption, and 6–8 distinct career destinations with sourced salary ranges and realistic entry barriers. Save `research/<slug>-research.md` before building the artifact. Flag uncertain or jurisdiction-dependent claims.
2. Build `artifacts/<slug>-roadmap.jsx` from that research; follow the reference's four-tab structure, expandable items, career cards, distinct field-specific design, responsive layout, standalone default export and optional `summary` prop. Inspect an existing roadmap as an implementation example, not a source of new facts.
3. If adding the field to the site, follow `README.md`'s new-roadmap checklist: catalog and unique icon, featured U.S. occupation and metrics, AI resilience profile and ledgers. Use `update-career-comparisons` to evaluate the new roadmap against **every existing comparison dataset**, retrieving the original sources listed in `docs/roadmap-metrics.md`. Add or link verified values and document why any dataset cannot support the occupation or surveyed major; never substitute an invented value. Use `research-ai-resilience` for the AI research. Preserve existing stable IDs.
4. Run the relevant data checks and `npm run build`; inspect affected pages, navigation, expandable cards and research downloads when browser access is available. Report the research and artifact paths, checks, and 3–4 useful findings, including any limits.

If the user requests research only, stop after delivering the research. If they request an end-to-end build, complete both stages without an unnecessary approval pause.
